fix: SSL Postgres FATAL could not load private key file Permission denied (#2)

* Initial plan

* fix: set SSL cert ownership before PostgreSQL container starts

PostgreSQL fails to start with 'FATAL: could not load private key file:
Permission denied' because the SSL private key (server.key) is owned by
root with mode 600, but the postgres user inside the Docker container
(UID 999 in official images) cannot read it.

The existing chown ran *inside* the container after startup via docker exec,
but by then PostgreSQL had already tried to read the key and failed,
causing a restart loop.

Fix: add host-level chown 999:999 and chmod commands BEFORE
docker compose up -d so the key is readable when PostgreSQL starts.

Also remove the unconditional chmod +x in LocalFileVolume.saveStorageOnServer()
that was applied to all files regardless of whether they needed it.

Co-authored-by: WolffM <8714327+WolffM@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: address review feedback on SSL cert permission handling

- Extract SSL permission commands into prepareSslCertificatePermissions()
  private method so tests can exercise the real implementation directly
- Use escapeshellarg() on SSL file paths to prevent shell metacharacter issues
- Remove 2>/dev/null || true error suppression to surface chown/chmod failures
- Rewrite unit tests using ReflectionMethod to call the private method directly
- Add docblock explaining UID 999 and why host-level fix must precede container start

Co-authored-by: WolffM <8714327+WolffM@users.noreply.github.com>

[expo-dev-menu] Fix app freeze when dismissing fullScreenModal (iOS) (#2)

* Initial plan

* Fix fullScreenModal freeze by replacing UIWindow.gestureRecognizers swizzling with notification-based approach

The root cause was DevMenuTouchInterceptor swizzling UIWindow.gestureRecognizers
and calling addGestureRecognizer inside the property getter. When UIKit internally
queried gestureRecognizers during a fullScreenModal dismissal transition, the
swizzled getter modified the gesture recognizer list mid-transition, causing the
app to freeze.

The fix replaces the swizzling with a notification-based approach:
- Registers for UIWindow.didBecomeKeyNotification to track key window changes
- Adds the gesture recognizer directly to the current key window on install
- Moves the recognizer when the key window changes (excluding DevMenuWindow overlay)
- Properly cleans up on uninstall

Co-authored-by: WolffM <8714327+WolffM@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address review feedback: main-thread safety, window-level filter, changelog format

- Dispatch UIKit mutations (add/remove gesture recognizer) to main thread when
  isInstalled is toggled off-main
- Filter didBecomeKeyNotification to only normal-level windows to avoid
  attaching the recognizer to system overlays (keyboard, alerts, etc.)
- Apply same windowLevel == .normal filter to addRecognizerToKeyWindow()
- Update CHANGELOG entry to match existing PR link + attribution format

Co-authored-by: WolffM <8714327+WolffM@users.noreply.github.com>

Fix: Conflicting values for `process.env.NODE_ENV` with Angular builders (#2)

* Initial plan

* fix: remove conflicting process.env.NODE_ENV from Angular CLI DefinePlugin

When using Angular builders, both Angular CLI's webpack config and Storybook's
base webpack config include a DefinePlugin that defines process.env.NODE_ENV.
Merging these configs causes webpack to warn about conflicting values.

Add a filterNodeEnvFromDefinePlugins utility that removes process.env.NODE_ENV
from Angular CLI's DefinePlugin instances before merging, letting Storybook's
DefinePlugin (which handles NODE_ENV properly) be the sole definition.

* fix: address review feedback on filterNodeEnvFromDefinePlugins

- Document in-place mutation in JSDoc and return plugins array for composability
- Handle nested 'process.env' object form ({ 'process.env': { NODE_ENV } })
  in addition to the flat 'process.env.NODE_ENV' key form
- Replace Record<string, any> with Record<string, unknown> in tests, remove as any casts
